example: Imagine equal NaCl concentrations on both sides of a phospholipid bilayer and a battery creating voltage across it. Without ion channels, membrane conductance is zero, so no ionic current crosses despite the electrical force.

en.title: The Cell Membrane as an Electrical Boundary
en.learning_objective: Explain why a neuronal membrane can separate electrical charge and why ions cross it only through suitable membrane proteins.
en.simple_explanation: A neuron's membrane is a phospholipid bilayer. Its nonpolar interior blocks water-soluble ions, so the fluids inside and outside can maintain different ion concentrations and electrical conditions.
en.how_it_works: The bilayer supplies the barrier. Selective ion channels form pores that let particular ions cross; gated channels can open or close. Ion pumps use energy from ATP to transport certain ions and help maintain unequal distributions. When a suitable channel is open, concentration and electrical gradients can drive ion movement.
en.visual:
outside: water + ions
════════ membrane ════════
       channel │ pump
inside:  water + ions
barrier + paths → controlled flow
en.use_case: Predict whether current crosses a membrane when voltage is present but no ion channels are available, then predict what changes when a selective channel opens.
en.expected_result: With no channels, conductance is zero and no ionic current crosses. Opening a suitable channel creates a path, although net flow still depends on a driving gradient.
en.what_to_notice: A driving force and a pathway are separate requirements. Voltage alone cannot move ions through an impermeable bilayer, and an open channel alone does not guarantee net movement.
en.common_mistake: Do not treat the membrane as a simple wall or assume every open channel passes every ion. Channel pore properties determine ion selectivity.
en.practical_tip: For any ion-movement problem, ask two questions in order: “Is there a permeable channel?” and “What concentration or electrical force drives the ion?”
en.question: Why can a neuronal membrane maintain electrical differences across it?
en.answer: Its phospholipid core blocks ions, while selective channels and ATP-driven pumps control when and how ions cross.
